title: Unit 5 · Family and friends
description: Family, relationships, appearance, possessives, free time, and agreeing about likes.
source: Original exercises aligned to the Aula Internacional Plus 1 Unit 5 syllabus; no textbook exercise text copied.

cards.prompt: La madre de mi madre es mi ___.
cards.translation: My mother's mother is my grandmother.
cards.note: La abuela is grandmother.

cards.prompt: El padre de mi padre es mi ___.
cards.translation: My father's father is my grandfather.
cards.note: El abuelo is grandfather.

cards.prompt: La hija de mis padres es mi ___.
cards.translation: My parents' daughter is my sister.
cards.note: La hermana is sister.

cards.prompt: El hijo de mis padres es mi ___.
cards.translation: My parents' son is my brother.
cards.note: El hermano is brother.

cards.prompt: La hermana de mi padre es mi ___.
cards.translation: My father's sister is my aunt.
cards.note: La tía is aunt.

cards.prompt: El hermano de mi madre es mi ___.
cards.translation: My mother's brother is my uncle.
cards.note: El tío is uncle.

cards.prompt: La hija de mi tía es mi ___.
cards.translation: My aunt's daughter is my cousin.
cards.note: La prima is a female cousin.

cards.prompt: El hijo de mi tío es mi ___.
cards.translation: My uncle's son is my cousin.
cards.note: El primo is a male cousin.

cards.prompt: Mi madre y mi padre son mis ___.
cards.translation: My mother and father are my parents.
cards.note: Los padres means parents as well as fathers.

cards.prompt: Ana tiene un hijo y una hija: tiene dos ___.
cards.translation: Ana has a son and a daughter: she has two children.
cards.note: Hijos can refer to sons or to children of mixed genders.
Mi is the singular possessive for my.

cards.translation: Clara and Luis are my friends.
cards.note: Mis is used before a plural noun.
Tu without an accent means your.
Su can mean his, her, your formal, or their.
Nuestra agrees with the feminine noun casa.
Nuestros agrees with the masculine plural noun amigos.
Alto agrees with a masculine singular person.
Baja agrees with a feminine singular person.
Joven becomes jóvenes in the plural.
Largo agrees with el pelo, not with the person.
Corto agrees with the masculine noun pelo.

cards.prompt: Ella es rubia y tiene el pelo ___.
cards.translation: She is blond and has blond hair.
cards.note: Rubio agrees with el pelo; rubia describes the woman.
Castaño is commonly used for brown hair.
Rizado means curly when describing hair.
Gafas is normally plural.
La barba is a beard.

cards.prompt: ¿___ es la mujer de la foto?
cards.translation: Who is the woman in the photo?
cards.note: Quién asks about a person.
Esta es introduces a woman or feminine noun.
Use gusta with a singular noun.
Use gustan with a plural noun.
También agrees with an affirmative statement.
Tampoco agrees with a negative statement.
A mí sí contradicts a negative statement.
A mí no contradicts an affirmative statement.

cards.prompt: En mi tiempo libre me gusta ___.
cards.translation: In my free time I like reading.
cards.note: After gustar, use an infinitive for an activity.

cards.translation: On Saturdays I go to the cinema.
cards.note: Ir al cine means to go to the cinema.

cards.translation: I like going out with my friends.
cards.note: Salir con amigos means to go out with friends.

cards.prompt: Mi hermana ___ música todos los días.
cards.translation: My sister listens to music every day.
cards.note: Escucha is the third-person singular of escuchar.

cards.translation: My father does sport on Sundays.
cards.note: Hacer is irregular: él hace.
Bailamos is the nosotros form of bailar.

cards.translation: I go on holiday with my family.
cards.note: Ir de vacaciones means to go on holiday.
Casada agrees with Ana; use estar for marital status.
